summary: A series of nutrition wellness workshops launched September 15, 2023 aims to demystify diet myths and promote balanced eating for every life stage. Sessions covered macronutrients, age-specific needs, the Power Plate method, label reading, dietary restrictions, supplements, mindful eating, and habit-building. The workshops also fostered a supportive community of wellness advocates.
one_line: Wellness workshops since September 2023 teach balanced nutrition across all ages, from macronutrients and the Power Plate to labels, supplements, and mindful eating.
key_facts: The nutrition wellness workshop series has been running since September 15, 2023, to demystify nutrition and promote a balanced diet for every stage of life.
The workshops are led by nutritionists such as Dr. Emily Forrest and veteran dietitian Scott Mitchell.
The inaugural workshop on September 20 was held at the Local Health Community Center, where Dr. Emily Forrest highlighted carbohydrates, proteins, and fats.
Carbohydrates are the body's primary energy source, proteins are building blocks for growth and repair, and fats support cell function and help absorb vitamins.
The October 5th session for parents and elder caregivers featured pediatric nutritionist Lisa Chang and occupational therapist Michael Thompson on changing nutritional needs with age.
The Power Plate method, introduced October 21st, makes half the plate fruits and vegetables, one fourth whole grains, and one quarter lean proteins.
On November 2nd, Scott Mitchell taught food label reading, including spotting hidden sugars, deciphering fats, and comparing sodium levels.
The November 18th session brought together allergy specialists and culinary experts to show balanced eating for vegan, lactose-intolerant, gluten-free, and food-allergic people.
On December 4th, pharmacist Jane Li advised aiming for a diet that provides all nutrients while guiding those needing supplements for health conditions or restrictions.
The December 27th workshop covered mindful eating: eating slowly, savoring each bite, and listening to hunger cues to improve digestion and prevent overeating.
The January 15th gathering gave attendees practical strategies, with take-home materials, meal planning ideas, and online follow-up sessions offered as ongoing support.
At the February 10th session, participants shared success stories and challenges, showing a community of wellness advocates emerging.
